summary: Jeanne Bliss advocates replacing or augmenting traditional job applications with an experiential task that reveals an applicant’s fit to a customer-centric culture. Using Amy's Ice Creams as a concrete example, the talk describes giving applicants a white paper bag to fill and return, a playful activity intended to surface personality and interaction style. The presenter links this approach to broader service principles by comparing the workplace environment to a vibrant, customer-facing space like Seattle Fish Market and by emphasizing moments of human connection as the core of reliability. The talk also highlights how a brand’s growth can emerge from genuine customer experiences and word-of-mouth, rather than solely from paid advertising, and cautions that tangible service cues must align with the overall experience (as illustrated by the hotel-room analogy).
title: White Paper Bag Hiring: A Customer-Centric Recruitment Demonstration
topics: bring the best self to work
customer journey: first impression, experience, feel, reliability
